checks.description: Rectangle with geometric + dimensional + origin constraints solves successfully (solver rc 0) and reports FullyConstrained (DoF = 0).
Editing DistanceX 4.0 -> 6.5 re-solves: width becomes exactly 6.5 while the height constraint still holds at exactly 3.0.
The top-right corner follows the edit exactly ((6.5, 3.0)) while the origin-anchored corners stay fixed.
Fully constrained tangency: the horizontal line is forced to y = +2.0 EXACTLY (distance from center equals radius; solver converges with FullyConstrained).

FINDING: an UNDERCONSTRAINED tangent sketch can converge (solve rc 0) with the line NOT yet at the tangency distance (observed y != |r|). Implication: Offisos adapters must treat solver success and geometric satisfaction as separate assertions, and constrain sketches fully before relying on tangency.
Perpendicular constraint solves the shared corner to exactly (4, 0) and the vertical edge end to exactly (4, 3).

With an Equal constraint, editing the single length datum 3.0 -> 5.0 changes BOTH lines to exactly 5.0 (before/after assertions; the solver may slide the unanchored line, so lengths are measured point-to-point).
Adding a second conflicting dimension on the same measured distance is detected: solver reports conflicts/redundancy (DoF changes, non-empty detection lists).
Zero and negative unsigned Distance datums are rejected with typed ValueError (no silent acceptance).
